questions.stem: In Aplysia, repeated gentle touches to the siphon reduce the gill-withdrawal reflex. The best cellular explanation is
options: reduced neurotransmitter release from the sensory neuron
increased serotonin release from a facilitating interneuron
desensitization of motor neuron receptors to transmitter
growth of new synapses through CREB-mediated transcription
questions.explanation: Short-term habituation reflects presynaptic depression, with less transmitter released by the sensory neuron. Serotonin from a facilitating interneuron underlies sensitization, motor receptors remain responsive, and CREB-dependent growth underlies long-term sensitization.

questions.stem: A patient's fear of dogs is extinguished in therapy but returns when the patient visits the original place of the dog bite. This is
questions.explanation: The CR returned when the CS was encountered in the acquisition context after extinction elsewhere, which is renewal. Reinstatement needs an unsignaled UCS, generalization needs a similar stimulus, and negative reinforcement is an operant concept.

questions.stem: A parent says, "Finish your homework, then you may play video games." This applies
questions.explanation: A more probable activity (games) is used to reinforce a less probable one (homework). The sleeper effect concerns persuasion, the matching law concerns choice among schedules, and no stimulus pairing is described.

questions.stem: To teach a pigeon to peck a disk that it never pecks spontaneously, a trainer should first reinforce
options: only full pecks at the disk
every response with a mild shock
questions.explanation: Shaping rewards successive approximations of the target. Waiting for a full peck gives nothing to reinforce, punishment would not build the response, and extinction removes reinforcement.

questions.stem: A student watches a demonstration of a surgical knot but cannot repeat it later because the steps are not remembered. Which of Bandura's processes failed?
questions.explanation: The learner noticed the demonstration but did not store the steps, so retention failed. Attention was adequate, motivation concerns incentive to perform, and reproduction concerns physical ability, which was not the problem described.

demo_cards.front: Why are habituation and sensitization called nonassociative learning?
demo_cards.back: The organism changes its response to a single stimulus without linking two stimuli or linking a response to a consequence.

demo_cards.text: A decline in response to a repeated, harmless stimulus is called {{c1::habituation}}, the simplest form of nonassociative learning.
demo_cards.extra: A decline in response to a repeated, harmless stimulus. It is the simplest form of nonassociative learning.

demo_cards.stem: After a loud crash, a person jumps at a quiet footstep. This is
demo_cards.why: A strong stimulus raised responsiveness to a different, weak stimulus. No stimulus pairing or consequence is involved, so it is nonassociative sensitization.

demo_cards.statement: Habituation requires pairing the repeated stimulus with a second stimulus.
demo_cards.why: Habituation involves a single repeated stimulus. Pairing two stimuli is classical conditioning.
